services.name: Apply for Employment Insurance (EI)
services.summary: EI gives temporary income to people who lost their job through no fault of their own, are sick, or are caring for someone. Apply online as soon as you stop working.

services.name: Apply for income assistance (welfare)
services.summary: If you cannot pay for food and shelter, your province or territory's income assistance program can help. In Ontario it is Ontario Works.

services.name: Canada Disability Benefit
services.summary: A monthly federal payment for working-age people (18 to 64) with a disability who have the Disability Tax Credit and a low income.

services.name: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (formerly the GST/HST credit)
services.summary: A tax-free quarterly payment for people with low and modest incomes. It replaced the GST/HST credit in July 2026. You get it automatically when you file your taxes.

services.name: Canada Pension Plan disability benefits
services.summary: A monthly payment for people under 65 who have paid into the CPP and cannot work regularly because of a severe and prolonged disability. In Québec, apply to Retraite Québec.

services.name: Canada Workers Benefit (CWB)
services.summary: A refundable tax credit for people and families working on a low income. Claim it on your tax return.

services.name: Disability Tax Credit (DTC)
services.summary: A tax credit that lowers the income tax of people with a severe and prolonged impairment, or the family who supports them. It also opens other programs such as the RDSP.

services.name: Disability income support from the province
services.summary: Provinces and territories pay monthly income support to people with a disability and a low income, such as ODSP in Ontario and AISH in Alberta.

services.name: Find unclaimed money
services.summary: The Bank of Canada holds forgotten bank balances; search for your name for free. Uncashed government cheques can be checked in your CRA account.

services.name: Get help with debt or bankruptcy
services.summary: The Office of the Superintendent of Bankruptcy explains your options, from consumer proposals to bankruptcy, and lists licensed insolvency trustees.

services.name: Veterans benefits and services
services.summary: Veterans Affairs Canada supports veterans, RCMP members and their families with disability benefits, health care, income support and transition help.

services.name: Book a road test or knowledge test
services.summary: Driving tests are booked with the province or territory's licensing service. Study the driver's handbook first.

services.name: Check road conditions and closures (511)
services.summary: Each province and territory publishes highway conditions, closures, construction and cameras, usually by 511 online and by phone.

services.name: Get an accessible parking permit
services.summary: People with a disability that limits walking can get a permit to park in accessible spaces. Who issues it depends on the province.

services.name: Get, renew or replace a driver's licence
services.summary: Driver's licences are issued by your province or territory. Who issues them differs: ICBC in British Columbia, registry agents in Alberta, SGI in Saskatchewan, Manitoba Public Insurance, ServiceOntario, the SAAQ in Québec.

services.name: Pay or dispute a parking ticket
services.summary: Municipalities issue and collect most parking tickets. Pay or dispute one through your municipality.

services.name: Public transit: routes, schedules and passes
services.summary: Buses, trains and transit passes are run by your municipality or a regional transit authority.

services.name: Register a vehicle and renew licence plates
services.summary: Vehicle registration and plates come from the same provincial service as driver's licences. Some provinces sell compulsory insurance with the registration.

services.name: Apply for student loans and grants
services.summary: Apply through your province or territory for student aid for college, university or trade school. In most of them, one application covers both provincial and federal loans and grants.

services.name: Canada Student Loans and Grants
services.summary: Federal student grants and loans for college and university. You apply through your province or territory, and repay through the National Student Loans Service Centre.

services.name: Get a high school transcript or diploma copy
services.summary: Depending on the province, transcripts come from the education ministry or from your last school or school board.

services.name: Register a child for school
services.summary: Public schools are run by school boards (school divisions or districts). Register with the board for your address; language and faith boards may overlap.

services.name: Save for a child's education (RESP and Canada Learning Bond)
services.summary: The government adds money to Registered Education Savings Plans. Families with low income can get the Canada Learning Bond, up to $2,000, without putting in any money.

services.name: School buses, delays and school closures
services.summary: School boards, or the transportation groups they run together, plan bus routes and announce delays, cancellations and closures.

services.name: Canada Child Benefit (CCB)
services.summary: A tax-free monthly payment for families with children under 18. Apply when your child is born or comes to live with you, and file your taxes every year to keep getting it.

services.name: Collect child or spousal support
services.summary: Each province's maintenance enforcement program collects court-ordered or agreed support and passes it on. In Québec, Revenu Québec collects support payments.

services.name: Find licensed child care or daycare
services.summary: Provinces and territories license child care centres and home daycares and publish where they are.

services.name: Get a marriage licence
services.summary: You need a marriage licence before the ceremony. Depending on the province, it comes from a municipal office, an issuer or a government office. In Québec, a notice of marriage is published instead.

services.name: Get help paying for child care
services.summary: Licensed child care costs less under the Canada-wide early learning and child care plan, and families with lower incomes can get more help. Apply through your province or territory, or in Ontario your local service manager.

services.name: Maternity and parental benefits
services.summary: Employment Insurance pays maternity and parental benefits while you are off work with a new baby or newly adopted child. In Québec, the Québec Parental Insurance Plan pays them instead.

services.name: Register a baby's birth
services.summary: Parents register a birth with the province or territory, usually within 30 days. Many provinces let you apply for the birth certificate, SIN and child benefits at the same time.

services.name: Report child abuse or neglect
services.summary: If you think a child is being abused or neglected, report it to child protection services. If the child is in immediate danger, call 911.

services.name: Apply for or renew your health card
services.summary: Public health insurance is run by each province and territory. Apply when you move there, renew when your card expires, and replace it if lost.

services.name: Canadian Dental Care Plan
services.summary: The Canadian Dental Care Plan helps cover dental care for residents who have no dental insurance and a family income below the plan's limit.

services.name: Check product, food and vehicle recalls
services.summary: The federal government publishes recalls and safety alerts for food, health products, consumer products and vehicles.

services.name: Find a family doctor or nurse practitioner
services.summary: Most provinces keep a waitlist that matches people without a family doctor to one who is taking patients.

services.name: First Nations and Inuit health benefits (NIHB)
services.summary: The Non-Insured Health Benefits program covers drugs, dental, vision, medical supplies, mental health counselling and medical travel for eligible First Nations and Inuit.

services.name: Get help in a mental health crisis (call or text 988)
services.summary: If you or someone you know is thinking about suicide, call or text 988, any time. It is free and confidential. In immediate danger, call 911.

services.name: Get help paying for prescription drugs (pharmacare)
services.summary: Each province and territory has a public drug plan, often for seniors, people on assistance, and anyone with high drug costs compared to income.

services.name: Go to an emergency room
services.summary: In a life-threatening emergency, call 911. Most hospitals have an emergency department that is open all day, every day.

services.name: Home care and community care
services.summary: Publicly funded home care brings nursing, personal support and therapy to people at home. Your health authority assesses what you need.

services.name: Register as an organ and tissue donor
services.summary: Each province and territory keeps its own way to record your decision to donate organs and tissue. Tell your family too.

services.name: See a doctor without an appointment
services.summary: Walk-in and urgent care clinics and community health centres see people without a family doctor or appointment.

services.name: Talk to a nurse (811 health line)
services.summary: Call 811 in most provinces and territories for free health advice from a registered nurse, any time.

services.name: Vaccines and immunization records
services.summary: Public health offices, pharmacies and clinics give publicly funded vaccines. Your province or territory keeps your immunization record.

services.name: Apply for social or affordable housing
services.summary: Rent-geared-to-income and affordable housing is run by provincial and territorial housing agencies, often through local housing providers. Waitlists can be long.

services.name: Check or appeal your property assessment
services.summary: Your property's assessed value sets your property tax. Depending on the province, a provincial agency or your municipality assesses it, and you can ask for a review if you disagree.

services.name: Get a building or renovation permit
services.summary: Your municipality issues building, renovation, demolition, deck, fence and pool permits, and inspects the work.

services.name: Renting: rules, rent increases, evictions and disputes
services.summary: Each province and territory sets the rules for renting and runs a board or office that settles disputes between landlords and tenants.

services.name: Save for and buy your first home
services.summary: The First Home Savings Account (FHSA) and the Home Buyers' Plan help first-time buyers save tax-free for a home.

services.name: Search or register a land title
services.summary: Each province keeps the official record of who owns land and what is registered against it. Searches usually cost a small fee.

services.name: Zoning, land use and development applications
services.summary: Your municipality sets zoning and decides rezoning, minor variance, subdivision and site plan applications.

services.name: Apply for Indian status or a status card
services.summary: Indigenous Services Canada registers people under the Indian Act and issues the secure certificate of Indian status (status card).

services.name: Change your address with the province
services.summary: Some provinces update your driver's licence, health card and other records in one step when you move. Elsewhere, update each one, and tell the CRA too.

services.name: Get a Social Insurance Number (SIN)
services.summary: You need a SIN to work in Canada and to get government benefits. Apply online, by mail or at a Service Canada office; it is free.

services.name: Get a photo ID card (if you don't drive)
services.summary: Most provinces and territories issue a government photo ID card for people who do not have a driver's licence.

services.name: Get or renew a passport
services.summary: Passports are issued by the federal government. Many adults can renew online; others apply by mail or at a Service Canada or passport office.

services.name: Get proof of Canadian citizenship
services.summary: A citizenship certificate proves you are a Canadian citizen. You can apply for one, or replace a lost one, from the federal government.

services.name: Legally change your name
services.summary: A legal name change is made through the vital statistics office of your province or territory. Taking a spouse's name after marriage usually does not need one.

services.name: Order a birth certificate
services.summary: Birth certificates come from the vital statistics office of the province or territory where the birth happened, wherever you live now.

services.name: Order a death certificate
services.summary: Death certificates come from the vital statistics office of the province or territory where the death happened. The funeral home usually registers the death.

services.name: Order a marriage certificate
services.summary: Marriage certificates come from the vital statistics office of the province or territory where the marriage took place.

services.name: Apply for Canadian citizenship
services.summary: Permanent residents who have lived in Canada long enough can apply to become citizens, take the citizenship test and attend a ceremony.

services.name: Check an immigration or citizenship application
services.summary: Check processing times and the status of an application with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

services.name: Claim refugee protection
services.summary: People in Canada who fear returning to their home country can make a refugee claim, online from inside Canada or at a port of entry.

services.name: Crossing the border: declare goods, duty and NEXUS
services.summary: The Canada Border Services Agency sets what you can bring into Canada and the duty you pay. It also runs NEXUS with the United States and posts border wait times.

services.name: Free help for newcomers: settlement services and language classes
services.summary: Federally funded organizations help permanent residents and refugees settle: jobs, housing, schools, and free English or French classes. In Québec, the province runs these services.

services.name: Get a study permit
services.summary: International students need a study permit to study in Canada for more than six months.

services.name: Get a work permit
services.summary: Most people who are not citizens or permanent residents need a work permit to work in Canada.

services.name: Get emergency help while outside Canada
services.summary: Canadians in trouble abroad can contact the nearest embassy or consulate, or the Emergency Watch and Response Centre at any time.

services.name: Immigrate through a province or territory
services.summary: Provinces and territories nominate immigrants for permanent residence through their own programs. Québec selects its own immigrants.

services.name: Immigrate to Canada (permanent residence)
services.summary: Express Entry and other federal programs lead to permanent residence. Provinces and Québec also select immigrants.

services.name: Renew or replace a permanent resident card
services.summary: Permanent residents renew or replace their PR card with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

services.name: Sponsor a family member to immigrate
services.summary: Citizens and permanent residents can sponsor a spouse, partner, dependent child, and in some cases parents and grandparents.

services.name: Travel advice and advisories
services.summary: Check the official travel advisory for any country before you go, and register as a Canadian abroad.

services.name: Visit Canada: visitor visa or eTA
services.summary: Most visitors need a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to come to Canada.

services.name: Apply for a record suspension (pardon)
services.summary: The Parole Board of Canada can order a criminal record kept separate, so it does not show in most checks, once you have finished your sentence and waited.

services.name: Complain about a business (consumer protection)
services.summary: Provincial and territorial consumer protection offices explain your rights and take complaints about businesses, contracts and scams.

services.name: Contact the police (non-emergency)
services.summary: In an emergency, call 911. For anything else, contact the police service for your area: a municipal force, or a provincial force or RCMP detachment under contract.

services.name: Emergency alerts and how to prepare
services.summary: Your province or territory's emergency management office issues alerts and evacuation orders for floods, wildfires and storms, and helps you prepare.

services.name: Get a criminal record check (police check)
services.summary: Police services for your area do criminal record and vulnerable sector checks for jobs and volunteering. Some can be done online.

services.name: Get a firearms licence (PAL)
services.summary: The RCMP's Canadian Firearms Program issues possession and acquisition licences, after a safety course, and registers restricted firearms.

services.name: Get legal aid
services.summary: Legal aid gives free or low-cost legal help to people with low incomes, mainly for criminal, family and immigration matters.

services.name: Make a human rights complaint
services.summary: If you faced discrimination at work, in housing or in services, complain to your province or territory's human rights commission or tribunal. Federally regulated employers and services go to the Canadian Human Rights Commission.

services.name: Report a scam or fraud
services.summary: Report scams, fraud and identity theft to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, and to your local police.

services.name: Sue for a small amount (small claims)
services.summary: Small claims courts and tribunals settle money disputes, such as unpaid bills, deposits or damage, without needing a lawyer. The limit differs by province.

services.name: Contact your municipality (311)
services.summary: Many cities answer questions and take service requests at 311; elsewhere, call or visit the town or city hall.

services.name: Drop off large items, electronics or hazardous waste
services.summary: Landfills, transfer stations and depots take what curbside collection does not: furniture, appliances, electronics, paint, batteries and chemicals.

services.name: Garbage, recycling and compost pickup
services.summary: Your municipality (or regional district) collects garbage, recycling and green bin waste. Check your collection day and what goes where.

services.name: Get a burning or fire permit
services.summary: Municipal fire departments issue permits for open-air and backyard burning. In forest areas and during fire bans, provincial rules also apply.

services.name: Get a dog or cat licence
services.summary: Most municipalities require dogs, and many require cats, to be licensed each year.

services.name: Get a library card
services.summary: Public libraries are free. A card gives you books, e-books, internet, programs and often free passes.

services.name: Get a residential or visitor parking permit
services.summary: Many municipalities issue on-street parking permits for residents and visitors.

services.name: Lost pets, stray animals and animal complaints
services.summary: Municipal animal services (or a contracted shelter) handle lost and found pets, strays, dog bites, barking and wildlife problems.

services.name: Pay your water and sewer bill
services.summary: Most municipalities bill for water and sewer service, often with a meter. Some bill it with property tax.

services.name: Report a noise or bylaw problem
services.summary: Municipal bylaw officers handle noise, property standards, long grass, illegal dumping, parking on lawns and similar complaints.

services.name: Report a pothole, streetlight or sidewalk problem
services.summary: Your municipality maintains local roads, sidewalks, streetlights and traffic signals. Provincial highways are the province's.

services.name: Report a water main break, sewer backup or boil water problem
services.summary: Your municipality runs the water and sewer system. Report breaks, no water, backups, flooding and water quality concerns.

services.name: Sign up for recreation programs and swimming lessons
services.summary: Your municipality runs pools, arenas, community centres and parks, with programs, lessons, camps and drop-in times.

services.name: Snow clearing and winter parking bans
services.summary: Your municipality plows and salts local roads and sidewalks, and announces snow routes and overnight parking bans.

services.name: Boating: operator card and pleasure craft licence
services.summary: You need proof of competency, such as a Pleasure Craft Operator Card, to drive a motorboat. Boats with motors of 10 hp (7.5 kW) or more also need a Pleasure Craft Licence from Transport Canada, which has a fee and lasts 5 years.

services.name: Buy a fishing licence
services.summary: Provinces and territories sell recreational fishing licences for fresh water. In British Columbia's tidal waters and some other fisheries, the federal government issues the licence.

services.name: Buy a hunting licence
services.summary: Hunting licences, tags and draws are run by each province or territory. First-time hunters need a hunter education course.

services.name: Register a drone and get a drone pilot certificate
services.summary: Every drone of 250 g or more must be registered with Transport Canada. Pilots of drones up to 150 kg need a drone pilot certificate.

services.name: Reserve a campsite in a provincial or territorial park
services.summary: Provincial and territorial parks take campsite and cabin reservations online. Popular parks book up the day reservations open.

services.name: Visit or camp in a national park
services.summary: Parks Canada runs national parks, historic sites and marine areas. Buy a pass and reserve campsites online.

services.name: Weather forecasts and alerts
services.summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada issues the official forecasts and weather warnings, plus air quality and UV.

services.name: Wildfire status and fire bans
services.summary: Provinces and territories track wildfires and set fire bans and restrictions on campfires and burning.

services.name: Apply for a long-term care home
services.summary: Publicly funded long-term care homes (nursing homes) are reached through an assessment by your health authority or home care program, not by applying to a home directly.

services.name: Canada Pension Plan (CPP) retirement pension
services.summary: A monthly pension for people who worked and paid into the CPP, from as early as 60. People who worked in Québec get the Québec Pension Plan from Retraite Québec.

services.name: Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)
services.summary: A monthly payment, on top of OAS, for seniors with a low income. The Allowance helps some people aged 60 to 64.

services.name: Old Age Security (OAS) pension
services.summary: A monthly payment from age 65 for most people who have lived in Canada for at least 10 years since age 18. Many are enrolled automatically.

services.name: Provincial income top-ups for low-income seniors
services.summary: Several provinces and territories add a monthly or yearly payment for seniors with a low income, on top of OAS and GIS.

services.name: File your income tax return
services.summary: File your personal tax return with the Canada Revenue Agency each spring, usually by April 30. Québec residents also file a separate Québec return with Revenu Québec.

services.name: Free tax clinics
services.summary: Volunteers at free tax clinics file simple returns for people with a modest income. Find a clinic near you.

services.name: Pay your property tax
services.summary: In most places your municipality bills and collects property tax. In New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and rural areas of some provinces, the province sends the bill.

services.name: Register for, file and pay GST/HST (business)
services.summary: Businesses that earn more than $30,000 a year must register for and charge GST/HST. In Québec, Revenu Québec administers the GST along with the QST.

services.name: Sign in to CRA My Account
services.summary: CRA My Account shows your tax returns, refunds, notices of assessment, benefit payments and RRSP and TFSA room.

services.name: Find your Member of Parliament (MP)
services.summary: Search by postal code to find your MP and how to contact their constituency office.

services.name: Find your mayor and city councillor
services.summary: Your municipality lists the mayor and council members, which ward you are in, and council meeting agendas.

services.name: Find your member of the provincial or territorial legislature
services.summary: Find your MLA (MPP in Ontario, MNA in Québec, MHA in Newfoundland and Labrador) and how to contact their office.

services.name: Request government records (access to information)
services.summary: Anyone can request records held by federal institutions under the Access to Information Act, or their own personal information under the Privacy Act. Provinces have their own laws for their records.

services.name: Vote in a federal election
services.summary: Elections Canada runs federal elections. Check that you are registered, find where to vote, and vote by mail or in advance.

services.name: Vote in a municipal election
services.summary: Your municipality runs elections for mayor and council (and often school trustees). Check the voters' list and where to vote.

services.name: Vote in a provincial or territorial election
services.summary: Each province and territory has its own elections agency. Check that you are registered and find where to vote.

services.name: Apply for a federal government job
services.summary: The Public Service Commission posts federal public service jobs and student programs on GC Jobs.

services.name: Become an apprentice or get certified in a trade
services.summary: Provinces and territories register apprentices, set trade exams and issue certificates of qualification, including the Red Seal.

services.name: Find a job (Job Bank)
services.summary: Job Bank is the federal government's free job board, with job alerts, wages and outlooks for every occupation.

services.name: Get a business number (BN)
services.summary: A business number from the Canada Revenue Agency identifies your business for GST/HST, payroll, import and export, and corporate tax.

services.name: Get a municipal business licence
services.summary: Many municipalities require a licence to run a business, a home-based business or a short-term rental.

services.name: Get help finding a job or training
services.summary: Provincial and territorial employment centres help with job searches, resumes, training and apprenticeships, for free.

services.name: Hire a temporary foreign worker (LMIA)
services.summary: Most employers need a Labour Market Impact Assessment from Employment and Social Development Canada before hiring a foreign worker.

services.name: Incorporate a business federally
services.summary: Corporations Canada incorporates businesses that want to operate under one name across Canada. You can also incorporate in your province.

services.name: Join the Canadian Armed Forces
services.summary: The Canadian Armed Forces recruit full-time and part-time (Reserve) members in more than 100 careers.

services.name: Register a business name or incorporate
services.summary: Register a sole proprietorship, partnership or business name with your province or territory, or incorporate there. Federal incorporation is a separate option.

services.name: Register a trademark, patent or copyright
services.summary: The Canadian Intellectual Property Office registers trademarks, patents, industrial designs and copyrights.

services.name: Report a workplace injury (workers' compensation)
services.summary: If you are hurt or become ill because of work, tell your employer and file a claim with the workers' compensation board of your province or territory.

services.name: Sell to the federal government
services.summary: CanadaBuys lists federal tenders and explains how businesses can register as suppliers and bid.

services.name: Unpaid wages after an employer's bankruptcy
services.summary: The Wage Earner Protection Program pays eligible workers wages owed when their employer goes bankrupt or into receivership.

services.name: Your rights at work: pay, hours, leave and firing
services.summary: Provincial and territorial employment standards set minimum wage, overtime, vacation, leaves and notice of termination. File a complaint if you are owed money. Federally regulated jobs follow the Canada Labour Code.

benefits.name: Canada Pension Plan (CPP)
benefits.note: Covers the CPP retirement pension and the CPP disability, children's and survivor benefits.

benefits.name: Canada Pension Plan disability benefits
benefits.note: Paid on the same dates as the CPP retirement pension.

benefits.name: Old Age Security (OAS) pension
benefits.note: The same dates apply to the Guaranteed Income Supplement and the Allowance.

benefits.name: Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)
benefits.note: Paid together with the Old Age Security pension, on the same dates.

benefits.name: Veteran disability pension
benefits.note: The federal calendar lists these dates under the veteran disability pension.

benefits.name: Canada Child Benefit (CCB)
benefits.note: Related provincial and territorial child benefits are paid together with the CCB on these dates.

benefits.name: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (formerly the GST/HST credit)
benefits.note: The January and April 2026 payments went out under the old name, the GST/HST credit.

benefits.name: Advanced Canada Workers Benefit (ACWB)
benefits.note: These are the advance payments of the Canada Workers Benefit, paid three times in 2026.

benefits.name: B.C. income assistance
benefits.note: Each payment is for the following month, so the December 16, 2026 payment covers January 2027.

benefits.name: B.C. disability assistance
benefits.note: Paid on the same dates as income assistance, each payment covering the following month.

benefits.name: Alberta Child and Family Benefit (ACFB)
benefits.note: Paid by the Canada Revenue Agency four times a year.

benefits.name: Alberta Income Support
benefits.note: These are direct deposit dates for the following month; cheques are mailed two business days earlier.

benefits.name: Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH) and Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP)
benefits.note: AISH, ADAP and Income Support share one schedule; each date pays for the following month.

benefits.name: Saskatchewan Income Support (SIS)
benefits.note: These are direct deposit dates for the following month; mailed cheques go out a few days earlier.

benefits.name: Saskatchewan Assured Income for Disability (SAID)
benefits.note: Same schedule as Saskatchewan Income Support; these are direct deposit dates for the following month.

benefits.name: Manitoba Employment and Income Assistance (EIA)
benefits.note: These are direct deposit dates for the following month's benefits; mailed cheques are dated a little later.

benefits.name: Ontario Trillium Benefit (OTB)
benefits.note: Combines the Ontario energy and property tax credit, the Northern Ontario energy credit and the Ontario sales tax credit, paid by the CRA.

benefits.name: Ontario Works
benefits.note: Each payment is for the following month, so the November 30 payment covers December 2026.

benefits.name: Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP)
benefits.note: Each payment is for the same month; the page lists the December 2026 date as to be confirmed.

benefits.name: Québec Social Assistance Program and Aim for Employment Program
benefits.note: The page gives these as the current year's dates without printing the year, and it was last updated October 1, 2026.

benefits.name: Québec Social Solidarity Program and Basic Income Program
benefits.note: All four Québec social assistance programs share one list of payment dates.

benefits.name: Québec Pension Plan (QPP)
benefits.note: Covers the QPP retirement pension and the disability and survivors' benefits paid by Retraite Québec.

benefits.name: Québec Family Allowance
benefits.note: Paid four times a year by default; families who ask for monthly payments follow a separate monthly list on the same page.

benefits.name: Nova Scotia Income Assistance
benefits.note: Each month's payment is delivered over three days near the end of the month before, so the list has three dates per month.

benefits.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Disability Benefit (NLDB)
benefits.note: Paid monthly by the Canada Revenue Agency for the province.
